title: L7 · Skeletal System
subtitle: Functions, bone cells, bone shapes and structure, homeostasis, fractures

lines.text: A baby has about 300 bones. An adult has **206**.
The skeleton also includes cartilage and ligaments. Ligaments connect bone to bone.
It has two divisions.
The **axial** skeleton is the skull, spine and rib cage.
The **appendicular** skeleton is the limbs and their girdles.
The skeleton has five functions.
**Support** for the body. **Protection** for the heart, lungs and brain.
**Movement**. Muscles pull on bones like levers.
**Storage** of minerals like calcium, and of fat in yellow marrow.
**Synthesis** of blood cells. That's hematopoiesis, in red marrow.
In an embryo, every bone has **red marrow**.
Children still have it in every bone.
Adults keep it in only a few places.
The ends of the femur and humerus, the vertebrae, ribs, pelvis and skull.
Elsewhere it becomes **yellow marrow**, which is fat.
**Osteoprogenitor** cells are bone stem cells. They become osteoblasts.
**Osteoblasts** are construction. They deposit calcium onto collagen.
**Osteocytes** are the general contractor. They maintain bone.
**Osteoclasts** are demolition. They break bone down and release calcium.
Osteoclasts have many nuclei.
The bone matrix is completely solid.
**Hydroxyapatite** is mineral salt. It makes bone hard. It's two thirds of the matrix.
**Osteoid** is mostly collagen. It makes bone strong. It's one third.
**Long** bones are longer than wide. All are in the limbs.
**Short** bones are box shaped: the carpals and tarsals.
**Flat** bones are thin: most of the skull, the ribs, sternum and scapulae.
**Irregular** bones are odd shaped: vertebrae and the coxal bones.
**Sesamoid** bones form in tendons. The patella is one.
Wormian bones are extra bones in skull sutures.
The **diaphysis** is the shaft.
The **epiphyses** are the ends. They form joints.
The **epiphyseal plate** is the growth plate. It's the only place bone grows in length.
In adults it becomes the epiphyseal line.
Articular cartilage covers the ends.
The **periosteum** wraps the outside. The endosteum lines the marrow cavity.
Compact bone is built from **osteons**.
The **central canal** carries vessels and nerves.
Perforating canals run sideways to connect them.
**Lamellae** are rings around the canal, for strength.
**Lacunae** are little lakes that hold osteocytes.
**Canaliculi** are little canals that carry nutrients and waste.
**Spongy** bone fills the ends of long bones and the inside of other bones.
It has no osteons. It is made of thin plates called **trabeculae**.
**Woven** bone is poorly mineralized and slightly flexible.
It's normal in children and abnormal in adults.
Most bones form inside hyaline cartilage. That's **endochondral** ossification.
Flat bones of the skull form in a fibrous membrane.
That's **intramembranous** ossification.
Bone is constantly broken down and rebuilt.
**Wolff's law**: bone is laid down where stress is higher.
**Vitamin D** from the skin helps absorb calcium from food.
**Calcitonin** from the thyroid moves calcium into bone.
**PTH** from the parathyroids moves calcium out of bone.
A simple fracture is closed. A compound fracture breaks the skin.
**Compression**: bone is crushed, like vertebrae in osteoporosis.
Depressed: pressed inward, typical of the skull.
**Comminuted**: three or more pieces. Impacted: one end driven into the other.
**Spiral**: from twisting. **Greenstick**: incomplete, in children.
Step one: a **hematoma**, a big clot, stops the bleeding.
Step two: a **fibrocartilage callus** connects the ends.
Step three: osteoblasts turn it into a **bony callus**.
Step four: **remodeling**. Osteoclasts remove the extra. It can take years.
**Osteoporosis** is a loss of bone quantity. Bones become porous.
**Rickets** is soft bone in children, from low calcium and vitamin D.
**Osteomalacia** is soft bone in adults.
Osteogenesis imperfecta, or **OI**, is brittle bone disease. The body can't make working collagen.
